question: Which region is the source of basaltic magma?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Upper mantle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The upper mantle is the region of the Earth's interior extending from the base of the crust to a depth of about 660 kilometers.

• Basaltic magma is typically generated in the upper mantle due to partial melting of peridotite.

• This region is composed mainly of silicate minerals rich in magnesium and iron.

• Geological processes such as decompression melting and the addition of volatiles can cause the formation of basaltic magma in this region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Transition region**

• The transition region is a part of the Earth's mantle located between the upper mantle and the lower mantle.

• It extends from about 410 to 660 kilometers in depth.

• This region is characterized by significant changes in mineral phases due to increasing pressure.

• **Lower mantle**

• The lower mantle lies between the transition region and the core-mantle boundary, extending from 660 kilometers to about 2,900 kilometers in depth.

• It is composed of minerals such as bridgmanite and ferropericlase, which are stable at high pressures.

• Basaltic magma does not typically originate in the lower mantle due to the extreme pressures and different mineral compositions.

• **The core**

• The Earth's core is divided into the outer core and inner core.

• The outer core is liquid and composed mainly of iron and nickel, while the inner core is solid.

• The core does not produce basaltic magma, as it is composed of metals rather than silicate minerals.
